content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged horse frame. Host frame: the horse sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature combining a common octopus and a horse. The horse's head is fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: horse body and legs with its own dense fur on the face, neck, shoulders, hips, legs, and tail; plain coat with no stripes or spots. From the common octopus, as parts and materials on the horse's own body: soft, color-changing skin with fine bumps in its own colors, grown from the skin as the horse's own covering over the belly, flanks, and back. It replaces the horse's dense fur there and conforms to the horse's body, sized to the horse's body and following its contours; every covered part keeps the horse's own length and shape. The dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face, neck, shoulders, hips, legs, and tail keep the horse's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (rocky coast): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing horse-octopus hybrid**
I'm shaping the creature around a clear horse silhouette with an uncluttered head and visible eyes, then layering color-changing, bumpy octopus skin over the belly, flanks, and back while keeping the fur on face, neck, shoulders, hips, legs, and tail.
**Designing horse-octopus hybrid**
I'm planning a natural history illustration of a full-body horse with octopus skin covering the belly, flanks, and back, keeping horse fur on the head, neck, legs, and tail, with countershading and fine papillae texture.
